narrative: Material PL2__MCB48083 exhibits smooth, high-volume daily demand averaging ~117,866 units with a CV of 0.24, indicating low relative variability well-suited to a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.58) around a mean of 1.59 working days, driving a combined lead-time demand standard deviation of ~111,534 units. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock and orders at minimum quantity (11,382), generating excessive ordering frequency and significant stockout risk. The recommended EOQ-based order quantity of 601,778 units with a safety stock of 183,509 units reduces total annual cost by over 95% while satisfying the 95% service level target within the storage capacity constraint.
warnings: Current SAP safety stock is 0 — no buffer protection against demand or lead-time variability.
EOQ (601,778) significantly exceeds MOQ (11,382); capacity gate applied: SS + OQ = 785,287 <= 843,693 — feasible.
13 demand outliers detected and winsorized at 1st/99th percentile.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV=0.24) with non-zero daily demand (100% non-zero fraction) and moderate lead-time variability is the textbook case for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. EOQ minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs; the reorder point incorporates a z-score safety stock targeting 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The capacity constraint (843,693 units) is binding in the sense that SS+OQ=785,287 which leaves only ~58,406 units of headroom. Any upward revision of safety stock (e.g., for a higher service level) must be checked against this ceiling.
